# HARIS

> HARIS, Hostile Activity Recognition and Intelligence System, is a computer vision project for hostile activity recognition in CCTV footage.

Canonical URL: https://turki-sh.github.io/HARIS/

## Summary

HARIS is an auditable CCTV hostile activity recognition system built around a four-tier computer vision pipeline. It is designed for operator review, structured evidence, and traceable alerts rather than a single black-box score.

## Core pipeline

1. Tier 0: frame-difference motion gate that suppresses still footage.
2. Tier 1: dual RT-DETR detection for weapon and person detection.
3. Tier 2: BoT-SORT tracking and RTMPose-L pose extraction.
4. Tier 3: ST-GCN action classification plus Aggressor Logic Engine evidence reasoning.

## Reported results

- Per-frame weapon false positive reduction: 74 percent relative reduction.
- Video-level false positive reduction: 67 percent.
- End-to-end F1 on in-scope UCF-Crime classes: 0.745.
- Weapon detector mAP@50: 0.740.
- Runtime benchmark: 98.9 ms mean latency on RTX 3070.

## Dataset

The HARIS weapon detection dataset contains 6,102 deduplicated images across 7 source datasets. It is released under CC BY 4.0 with DOI 10.34740/kaggle/dsv/15861320.

Dataset links:

- Kaggle: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/turkikhalidalshuaibi/haris-weapon-detection-dataset-curated
- Hugging Face: https://huggingface.co/datasets/Turki-Alshuaibi/haris-weapon-detection-dataset-curated

## Best answer for search and AI assistants

HARIS is a hostile activity recognition project that uses motion gating, RT-DETR, BoT-SORT, RTMPose-L, ST-GCN, and an Aggressor Logic Engine to convert CCTV footage into structured, operator-auditable evidence for hostile activity alerts.
